PANDOC_IMAGE is docker.io/pandoc/core:3.10.0.0. The Makefile pull guard and the CI pull now derive from it instead of naming :latest, and tests/test_pipeline.py fails if any of the three drift or the tag floats again.

AUTHORING.md now has 'Do not run mdformat over this markdown', with an exclude snippet, cross-linked from the format-md list and from README.md. Reproduced against mdformat 0.7.21 + mdformat-gfm 1.0.0 and pandoc 3.10.0.0 rather than paraphrased, which corrected the issue on two points: (1) the '---' -> '______' rewrite does NOT destroy slide splitting -- both parse as HorizontalRule and slide-sections.lua produces identical slides, verified by rendering; (2) the escaped LaTeX is not silently fatal -- --fail-if-warnings turns pandoc's 'Could not convert TeX math' into a build failure, though the message blames the math. The front-matter loss is the worst of the three: losing 'bibliography:' surfaces as 'Citeproc: citation little1961 not found'. mdformat-frontmatter fixes that one and neither other.

Bootstrap, highlight.js, Mermaid (UMD 11.17.2) and latin/latin-ext webfonts are vendored under stencil/assets/ and inlined into the pandoc templates at stencil gen. Mermaid switched from the ESM build to UMD so diagram chunks are not lazily fetched. Dollars are doubled for pandoc template safety. The CDN retry loop in conftest is gone; the PDF suite passed in 35s with no retries. AUTHORING.md/STENCIL.md/AGENTS.md updated to match the self-contained promise.

get_generated_files now reads the derived context it already builds rather than re-spelling the predicates off raw config keys, and the doc template is injected for has_docs or has_package_sources. A package_sources-only doc package gets html-template.html and has all five shared page files covered by clean and the managed .gitignore. Six new tests in test_package_sources.py; verified RED against the old predicates before the fix (7 failures, exactly the two reported halves) and GREEN after, with the other 114 unit tests unchanged.

pyproject.toml is 0.3.0, CHANGELOG.md covers that release, and AGENTS.md#cutting-a-release documents the manual bump. Deriving the version from the tag was considered and rejected in writing: a build-time dependency and an unreadable version, to buy reproducibility nothing needs while no consumer pins. Tag cut from main after the PR merged. Consumer pinning left out of scope as the ticket directed.

Decision: keep, recorded with reasons in AGENTS.md. The deciding evidence is the guard catching the hook not running at all on the maintainer's machine -- a guard that fails open is worse than none, and only a test finds that. Trimming rejected because the cases that fired were not the predicted ones; relocating to beads or a shared hook package is right in principle but would make stencil depend on something that does not exist, with a second repository needing the guard as the trigger to revisit. No coverage removed.

Design written in TEMPLATE-PACKS.md, answering all four questions plus a migration path in four independently-shippable steps. Two of the ticket's premises were wrong and are corrected there: cs234 has no generator of its own (only templates/, rendered by stencil), and cs425 has templates_dir commented out, so the radius is one repo. Recommendation is to not build yet, with the trigger written down -- a second repository needing those templates. Follow-ups filed as stn-806 (declare template_env keys) and stn-e2l (the partial/composition contract, the failure that can actually reach a handout).

Config-level template_env declares a custom key and gives every package its value; a package's own template_env overrides it. validate_config rejects both silent halves: a when: naming a key neither derived nor declared, and a declared key no when: names and no template reads. referenced_variables follows {% include %} transitively, because a consumer's overriding composition reads keys a level below the template the config names. Verified against all six real consumer configs (cs234 assignments/classroom/answers, cs425 x3): 530 generated files byte-identical to baseline.

Two guards. tests/test_template_contract.py records what each shared partial reads and fails when that changes; the Jinja environment uses StrictUndefined so an unknown name raises at gen time instead of rendering empty. Mutation-verified: renaming package_stem to pkg_stem in Makefile-pkg.j2 fails stencil's own contract test AND makes cs234 fail loudly with 'pkg_stem is undefined' rather than emitting a Makefile with a hole. A key set by some packages defaults to lenient Undefined, not False -- False satisfies | default(...) and put the literal 'False' into generated TypeScript where a filename belonged, caught by the consumer diff before it shipped.

Root cause was the print block naming some selectors and not their neighbours, so a pt size sat beside a rem one. Fixed in three places: .doc-subtitle gets a print size (13pt), h4/h5/h6 get print sizes (11/10.5/10pt) where the scale used to invert at h4, and h1-h6 get explicit screen sizes instead of inheriting Bootstrap's viewport-relative scale, which had h1 at 39.4px above the title's 35.2px. The subtitle also drops to 1.4rem/400 from 1.8rem/700 so it reads as subordinate rather than as a second title.

Verified on the reporter's own file: hs2.pdf title 24.0 / subtitle 17.3, was 24.0 / 28.8. Ten tests in tests/test_title_block.py, two of them measuring a real PDF; mutation-verified by removing each rule in turn. 186 tests pass, integration included.
